target_customer: Large manufacturers that run fleets of forklifts, cranes and hoists
problem: Manufacturers lack analytics on the health and usage of industrial equipment fleets, so maintenance and purchasing decisions are made blind.
business_model: B2B SaaS analytics and fleet dashboards (pricing not found)

founders.name: Michael McHugh
previous_startups: Nomad Rides (YC S19), rideshare for campus towns, per his YC profile
founders.background_notes: Dealroom is said to describe both founders as Indiana University classmates, but that page was not opened and mixes in a ride-hailing company, so education is left null.

competitors.name: I.D. Systems (PowerFleet)
competitors.what: Forklift and industrial vehicle telematics, launched a lower cost solution for smaller operations

technical_complexity.rationale: Equipment analytics needs sensor or telematics data capture and dashboards. No source describes the build in detail.

defensibility.rationale: Incumbent telematics vendors already sold fleet data; no proprietary data or integration lock-in is documented.

market_need_then: Telematics vendors were pushing fleet visibility products down to smaller operations in early 2019, which suggests demand for equipment analytics. No direct evidence of Blockstamp customer demand found.

branding.domain_note: Uses blockstampsf.com, a city suffix variant, not blockstamp.com (site fetched 2026).

identity.voice_and_tone: Current site uses a plain tagline, Connected systems for industrial operations.

brand_strength.rationale: No press or community about the brand found. The name shares its words with blockchain timestamping projects, which a name search surfaces instead.

pivots.from: Asset management analytics for industrial equipment fleets
pivots.to: Custom industrial software and AI workflows (Blockstamp AI)
pivots.why: Not stated. The current site shows the change but gives no date or reason.

outcome_analysis: YC lists Blockstamp as inactive, but its own website is live in 2026 and sells custom industrial AI software, so the company appears to have continued under a different offering rather than shut down. No shutdown note, acquisition or post-mortem was found, and the cause of any failure of the original fleet analytics product is not public. No failure factors are assigned.
notes: The YC page lists founding year 2022 and a nomadrides GitHub link, which conflicts with the 2019 batch. The Dealroom page rests on a single database and appears contaminated (its description is for Nomad Rides and its funding table lists $125k at $2.0m and $1.8m seed), so the $150,000 round is unverified beyond that one database and is recorded as other. CB Insights lists the company as alive while YC says inactive. Loot-Drop suggests a shutdown with no detail. Competitor list reflects one dated source; no others dated near the batch were found.
